mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate over three months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over six months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of declining consumption expenditures (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate hike above 4.5% triggers a tightening regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of tightening above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both unemployment rate and payroll employment over three months signals a labor market normalization that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of simultaneous UNRATE decline and PAYEMS rise (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over six months signals economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures and housing starts over six months signals weakening demand, which reduces earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 2% AND HOUST falls > 5% in 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of simultaneous RSAFS and HOUST declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 7% signals a recessionary regime that reduces earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE > 7% (t-test p > 0.05).
